_about: KnowUS source policy (owner's editorial rule, Nov 9 2026). Edit this file to change what the app may cite. A source URL is allowed only if its domain (or a parent domain) is in an allowed group below, matches official_patterns, or is the person's own campaign/official site. Everything else (any other news outlet) is treated as banned. web.archive.org links are judged by the archived URL.

pending._how: Owner decided Nov 9 2026 5:51 PM: AP, Reuters and Wikipedia are banned. Set a value to "keep" to allow it again (one-line change).

groups_kept._how: set a group to false to stop allowing it

_about_groups: official_extra = government bodies on .com/.org; party_sites = official party organizations and legislative caucus sites; campaign_sites = candidates' own sites (plus each person's own site is always allowed); social_own_accounts = a person's own social posts; reference_non_news = vote/election databases, books, archives, libraries (not news media); orgs_non_news = advocacy groups, think tanks, unions, universities, companies quoted as primary sources for their own statements/ratings; app_and_data_services = sign-in, maps, open legislative data, the app's own data repo, file hosting used by official bodies (e.g. the Colorado legislature's bill files on s3) and newsletter sign-up forms officials link to. Set a group to false in groups_kept to stop allowing it. local_gov_sites = cities', towns', counties' and townships' own official websites that are not on .gov (checked: the site loads and names the place).

democratic_sources._about: Owner's rule, Nov 9 2026 8:58 PM: no Democratic sources anywhere in the app. Covers Democratic members' house.gov/senate.gov sites (current and former, from the congress-legislators party data), Democratic caucus/leadership/committee-minority sites, party organisations (DNC, DCCC, DSCC, DGA, state parties), Democratic officials' campaign sites and official social accounts, and the office sites of Democratic governors and statewide officials (by party in our data). State election offices (Secretary of State results pages) are not on this list: they are official election results, not a person's site.
democratic_sources._allow_own_site_for_dems: Pending owner's answer: true keeps a Democrat's OWN official/campaign site or account on that same person's OWN page (or own entry in a list). Set to false to ban those too (one-line switch).
democratic_sources._name_token_pattern: any host label matching this (e.g. senatedems, housedemocrats, mainedems, democrats-judiciary) is a Democratic party/caucus site
democratic_sources._caucus_hosted_own_pages: Democratic legislative leaders whose official member page is hosted on their caucus site: allowed only on that person's own page (and only while allow_own_site_for_dems is true).

removed_references._about: Owner's rule (Nov 10 2026): no Wikipedia-like references or news archives. Removed from reference_non_news.

social_accounts._about: Social media posts are allowed only from the page person's OWN account (handle matched below, by platform). Any other account is not a source.

ballot_refs_allowed._about: Owner (Shmuel), Nov 9 2026 10:30 PM ET: "I said to ban leftist biased things not unofficial sources." Ballotpedia and BallotReady are allowed again (reference_non_news).

narrow_exceptions._about: Narrow exceptions to a ban. A host listed here stays banned everywhere EXCEPT the one use named in 'only_for'. Checkers pass that use as the context (policy.py ok(..., context='house_call'); sources.js cls(url, own, person, 'house_call'); audit/policy.mjs cls(url, own, who, 'house_call')).

apnews.com.where: Elections tab only: the 'Called by AP' source link on a US House district race call (election-official.json house.states.*.districts[].callSrc, callBy 'AP'). Everywhere else AP stays banned (see pending: apnews.com ban).
apnews.com.owner: Shmuel, 12:34 AM ET Nov 10 2026, answering 'Use AP's House calls?': "Sure but only in the elections tab"

_added_2026_11_11_contacts: Added Nov 11 2026 (link-check fix after the contacts data, data/contacts/): scripts/sources_check.py now checks each contact block as that person's OWN record, the same way the app's ct blocks were already checked: the block's w (their own official or campaign site) and s (their own social accounts; for a local official, the town or county government's own official accounts) are allowed in that block only. A Democrat's own member page on a caucus host (housedemocrats.wa.gov/Hansen, housedems.com/tullio-liberati, assemblydems.com/...) counts only in that member's own block and never as the caucus home page, per the owner's rule (Nov 9 2026 9:18 PM: Democrats' own official/campaign sites on their own pages only). A block's contact form (f) on a form platform (AccessGov, SimpliGov, Formstack, CivicPlus, Revize, Salesforce sites, Microsoft Forms and the like) is judged by the official page that links to it (the block's src), like photos are judged by their page; only a form whose src is itself an allowed official or local-government page passes, and a form on a banned host stays banned. A candidate's second campaign domain named after them (electsandravanscotter.com for Sandra Van Scotter) is their own site. campaign_sites ihatepolitics.com (Codiga for Congress, NC-12), jessforcongress.com (Jessica Arriaga for Congress, PA-2), unfilteredwithteriann.org (Teri Ann Hourihan, AZ governor candidate), checked: the site loads and names the candidate. No banned or pending entry was changed.
